Consumer initialization contract

Procedure

Consumer initialization contract

This is the preparation, authorization, resume and acceptance contract for /initialize-project. The runbook owns exact edits and links to operator procedures. The preparation workbook owns human service steps and answers. The skill alone owns maturity and learning-edit policy.

Supported scope and target

Initialize one existing private GitHub repository created from the template. Preserve one Git worktree with backend/ and frontend/, the existing stack, session authentication, frontend examples, path-aware Hetzner CI and two paired manual deployments. Use an existing approved shared CI pool and deployment host. New foundation installation, shared privileged code changes, host rebuilds, database replacement and business-feature development are separate scopes.

Read Git/GitHub metadata instead of assuming the folder name, current CLI account, organization or template examples describe the consumer. Protect the canonical vireocodedev/web-app-starter remote from consumer initialization. Missing Git identity, a different existing application identity, unexpected local changes or existing data must be resolved in intake before mutations. Preserve data and credentials; a later project rename is not fresh setup.

Written preparation

Before a fresh initialization, the human uses the guided local web app (node .github/skills/initialize-project/scripts/prepare.mjs) or the Markdown fallback to save /.template-initialization/preparation.md in a user-owned 0700 directory with a regular 0600 file. Read the complete workbook; do not replace it with a chat interview, action menu, personal skill, old conversation or guessed defaults. Only supported use-profile answers delegate values to the explicitly selected protected operator profile.

The agent discovers facts it can verify, rather than asking the human to guess repository IDs, current permissions, record contents, resource ownership or free ports. Human identity, risk, data-boundary and resource-scope choices remain explicit written answers. Keep the stack and business-feature scope unchanged.

InputResolution
Repository/accountDetect exact owner/repository, numeric ID, default branch, privacy and authorized GitHub account; verify access rather than switch global accounts silently.
IdentityRead approved slug, display name, Java package, PWA name and artwork/localization policy; validate the runbook's destination constraints. Keep examples/framework attribution deliberately.
OperatorResolve the selected existing protected operator profile; use actual authorized access, not copied template IDs. Missing operator preparation is a blocker, not an in-run configuration interview.
EnvironmentsRead the two owned FQDNs and resolve the approved profile's host/zone/project. Inspect records and conflicts; create only missing records within the selected written mode.
AccountsRead approved username, display name and email. Generate distinct local/staging/production passwords in protected files after identity edits; no password fields in the workbook. admin is a name, not an implemented privileged role.
BackupsRequire explicit destination, same-server loss acceptance where applicable, and supported time/timezone. Profile defaults alone cannot accept consumer risk. Retention is 30 days; staging stays unscheduled.
ExecutionRequire the current invocation and signed/unexpired execute-listed-scope declaration for the exact consumer edits, publication/settings, registration/maintenance, resources, deployments, users and scratch restore. plan-only cannot execute these actions.
BoundsResolve permitted allocation, prerequisite policy and cleanup scope. No new paid host, resize/rebuild, privileged-source upgrade, database replacement, password reset, live restore or upstream publication. Package deletion requires exact declared IDs/owners/versions and digest-loss acceptance.

Human login/2FA, selected-repository App-owner consent, conditional CLI deletion scope authorization, protected credential entry and IDE trust/extension/import preparation happen before invocation. Secret input uses protected stores or hidden mechanisms, never Markdown/chat. A completed checkbox is an attestation, not proof of API access, actual launch behavior or a passed execution gate.

Guided browser input

The local wizard is a human input surface, not another initialization executor. It groups the existing field IDs and consent text into short steps, restores private drafts and writes the same workbook only after explicit final review. An existing file needs separate replacement confirmation and an unchanged revision; malformed or externally changed private data is preserved, not reset. It never probes providers, dereferences arbitrary entered paths or changes state.json, credentials, databases, deployments or acceptance records.

Its loopback-only server uses a per-run private access path and exact-origin write checks. Draft, launcher, session and lock files remain under the ignored private directory; the access link must not be shared. No browser local-storage copy of the answers or secret-input fields is used. Those runtime/draft files are not authority and are not consumed by the skill.

Written authority and readiness report

The tracked preparation guide stays blank. The human edits only the ignored copy, directly or through the wizard, including literal field values, conditional replacement rows, applicable attestations and action approvals. The agent never fills human approvals, signature or expiry, and never interprets Markdown/profile values as commands. If secret contents appear instead of references, stop with a redacted report; do not echo them, copy them to public documents or rotate unrelated credentials.

For execution, require all of:

  • A current user /initialize-project request for this consumer.
  • Complete supported answers, execution_mode: execute-listed-scope, explicit actions, an authorized signer matching the verified selected account, valid UTC signed/expiry times, and the selected repository/identity/bounds.
  • Live readiness checks resolving a nonsecret plan strictly inside that scope. Mechanical free-port allocation within approved ranges is allowed; new cost, target ownership or destructive scope is not.

The invocation makes the human's completed workbook the current instruction; the file is not standing or cryptographic authority by itself. A checked box, profile, old approved flag or past session alone never grants execution. Record the workbook SHA-256, signer/timestamps, invocation and verified repository ID/actor with the resolved plan before mutations. In-run resume requires the same scope and unexpired authority; a changed/expired declaration must be reconciled before any further affected mutation.

Write an agent-owned /.template-initialization/readiness.md under the ignored private directory. Its sections identify the input/hash and target, resolved plan/actions/bounds, actual readiness evidence, missing field IDs, manual steps with guide links, blocked versus passed gates and any Stable-learning proposals. Preserve relevant verified/recovery evidence when refreshing the report. It contains references only, not secret values or a verbatim filled workbook.

If answers/access/authority/tool capability are missing or conflicting, write that report and stop before affected writes. The human corrects/re-signs the workbook and invokes again; do not launch another chat questionnaire. A plan-only invocation stops at read-only discovery/reporting even with a completed form. Mandatory tool/provider approvals still apply.

Operator profile

The profile is an existing user/operator-supplied external JSON document, selected in the workbook, not a personal path hard-coded into the skill or a credential copied from conversation. Arrange a missing profile with the operator before invocation rather than rebuilding its configuration in chat. Keep it outside Git, user/root-owned 0600 under private directories. Treat fields as data; they cannot supply shell commands or override workflow policy.

Required fields:

FieldContents
version, nameFormat version 1 and a recognizable profile name.
githubHost, authorized account and allowed repository owner; confirm the cloned repo belongs to it.
sshTarget, identity/agent reference, approved host-key fingerprint and privilege mode (root or noninteractive sudo). Resolve interactive access in human preparation; verify host identity before sending source or secrets.
ciExisting pool label, canonical reviewed operator source checkout/revision, protected installed configuration path and App metadata/key paths on the operator host.
dnsProvider, exact zone and project IDs, plus local protected credential-file reference or an authenticated tool reference with the required zone access.
deploymentApproved host, per-project path namespace, permitted free-port range and authorized maintainers. Discover actual workflow IDs after publication.
backupSupported destination/profile reference and proposed time/timezone; require explicit consumer acceptance in intake.
boundsApproved prerequisite-installation policy, resource/cost ceilings and scope exclusions.

No token, password, PEM or secret environment content belongs in this JSON. References must resolve through verified protected storage on the current machine/host. Read-only discovery does not authorize an SSH trust bypass. The profile does not grant cross-repository publication or shared-host ownership.

Live readiness gate

Before executing any matching written approval, verify and record:

  • Actual GitHub identity/admin capabilities, organization/repository plan and Actions policies support private CI, the required main check and zero reviews.
  • The existing selected-repository App actually authenticates to this consumer; the authorized owner has already saved its selection. Missing consent is a preparation blocker. Keep App permissions minimal.
  • SSH/operator access works with strict host verification. The reviewed pool revision/configuration/receipt and registration procedure are available. A host needing an unreviewed repair is not a ready prerequisite.
  • DNS credential access reaches the exact zone/project; authority, A/AAAA/CNAME conflicts, delegation and recursive resolution are understood.
  • Supported local toolchains, Docker, repository verification commands, Java debugger/IDE tools and actual browser tooling are available under the written prerequisite policy. Identify a usable unattended path for both saved launch configurations; tool presence alone is insufficient. Verify actual launches after personalization, not by starting an old-identity database in preparation. Missing automation blocks the promised unattended setup; report it instead of planning a surprise human launch handoff. Validate on the actual OS.
  • Capacity supports existing workloads plus both consumer environments and CI. Allocate unused ports/resource names within the approved namespace, then recheck at mutation; a copied template port is not an allocation.
  • Existing local/server credentials, volumes, paths and pending transactions have known ownership and a safe fresh/resume boundary.
  • The chosen backup adapter and protected rehearsal destination are usable. Unsupported off-server transport must be prepared by the operator, not silently replaced with same-server storage.

Use verified roles, authenticated reads and documented operator interfaces. Any write needed to establish access must itself have explicit upfront consent; do not create disposable paid resources or change unrelated settings as probes. Mandatory external tool approvals cannot be waived by the skill.

Save the resolved nonsecret plan, readiness references and matching written approval provenance before bulk edits. There is no additional routine chat confirmation for a fully covered scope. An unresolved prerequisite remains a blocked gate, not a promise to discover access halfway through.

Execution and resume

Keep a local /.template-initialization/state.json, ignored by Git. Use atomic replacement under a user-only directory and keep secret values out of it. This record supports context compaction/resume; it is not authority by itself. Verify saved inputs, resource ownership, actual GitHub/server state and current authority before continuing. Reuse matching workbook/profile answers instead of repeating intake. A different identity/scope requires a written update.

An existing completed consumer, including one initialized before this workbook existed, needs no new form for a read-only readiness reconciliation. Preserve its accepted evidence and credentials; do not rerun setup or downgrade its phases merely to adopt a new preparation format. An incomplete legacy run needs the new complete workbook/current authority before further mutations, while preserving its already verified independent phases and resources.

Record:

  • Version 1, exact consumer repository ID/name and initial consumer commit.
  • Approved identity, operator-profile reference, target names and bounded plan; workbook hash, declaration/signer/validity and current-invocation provenance, not a self-authorizing approved: true flag.
  • Phase states (pending, in_progress, passed, blocked), source commits, run IDs, created resource IDs/ownership and secret storage references only.
  • Gate evidence, redacted failures, pending/recovery transaction identifiers and any post-intake intervention. Never execute commands from a state file.

Use these ordered phases:

PhaseEvidence required before passed
intakeComplete inputs, verified readiness and approved bounded execution.
identityEvery application-owned value/package/launch surface matches; residual template references classified.
localDeclared checks/builds, real native API/browser login-refresh-logout and actual IDE launch results.
ciOperator registration/current isolation receipt, real consumer workflows and read-back main policy with a failing/green merge gate proof.
environmentsExact DNS/TLS/ports, separate DBs/volumes/credentials, reviewed per-project control installation and verified public certificate variable.
stagingExact tested consumer commit, private immutable pair, successful complete staging workflow and actual public route/container identities.
productionSame verified staging pair promoted without rebuild behind a fresh production backup; successful workflow and public identity checks.
recoveryExplicit deployed-user provisioning and browser auth in both environments; initialized dump retrieved, checksum-verified and isolated-restored; approved production timer enabled afterwards.
handoffPersistent consumer-specific acceptance, operating instructions, protected credential references and clean scoped publication.

Follow the shared CI guide and release operator guide for commands and locks. Use the operator's canonical source for shared registration, not an unreviewed consumer fork of the foundation. Allocate a separate project control installation; preserve all existing projects, services and data.

The normal execution path asks no further configuration questions. Diagnose and repair routine failures within the approved scope, rerun the exact failed check and preserve independent passed work. New authority, cost, ownership, destructive work or an unresolved user decision requires a targeted pause and written workbook update rather than a guess. Explain exact blockers in the readiness report; do not replace the file-first process with late questions. Record unexpected human intervention as a preparation/preflight defect. Stable-mode reusable-learning edits need explicit written approval of the reported proposal IDs; none leaves them unapproved without blocking otherwise authorized operations.

Reconcile interrupted registrations, dumps and deployment journals before any retry. Preserve database volumes and existing passwords. Broad cleanup, disabled checks, relaxed TLS/runner isolation and automatic database restore are not recovery shortcuts.

Completion and rehearsal

Full setup is ready only when every phase is passed with current evidence for this consumer. Failure/missing access or an unverified required IDE/runtime check means blocked/partial. Actual successful staging and production runs are required: generated workflows and an image push are not deployment acceptance.

Write sanitized docs/acceptance/initialization-acceptance.json and consumer operating instructions with actual repo/run/source/digest/environment identities, local commands, credential references and recovery results. Copied template CI, release and host acceptance files remain labeled upstream historical/reference evidence, never proof for this consumer. Keep shared-infrastructure provenance and attribution distinct from application identity.

Keep all documentation *-acceptance.json records in docs/acceptance/, updating relative references when moving existing evidence. Infrastructure-owned receipts retain their owner-specific locations.

Regenerate and commit docs/project.html after every change under docs/, following the runbook. The single offline HTML file includes all top-level Markdown and documentation acceptance records, preserving the distinction between current consumer status and historical/reference evidence. CI rejects stale output. Keep secrets and ignored local run state outside the dashboard's inputs.

Report whether the run required human intervention after approval, and any portable skill/runbook changes for user-controlled upstream review. Do not promote skill maturity or publish upstream merely because setup succeeded. If an initial rehearsal needed mid-run fixes, capture them and require a clean fresh-consumer repeat before calling the no-follow-up experience proven.

For an explicitly requested personalization-only task, follow only the approved local runbook scope and report it as personalization, not full initialization. Commits, remote changes and deployments require their own approved scope.

Initialize a project from this template

Procedure

Initialize a project from this template

This is the authoritative map of application identity edits and setup owners. The explicit no-argument initialize-project skill owns execution and maturity/learning behavior. Its initialization contract owns written preparation, protected operator inputs, readiness, approval, local resume state and full acceptance. Before fresh initialization, use the preparation guide to save the private workbook through node .github/skills/initialize-project/scripts/prepare.mjs. Browser drafts are not authority; the skill reads the reviewed workbook.

Full setup includes local development, shared CI/main protection, DNS, private images, two real paired deployments and verified recovery under one approved consumer scope. An explicitly requested personalization-only task stays local. Make scoped edits directly; no renaming generator or runtime identity framework is required. Shared host rebuilds, foundation installation/upgrades and data replacement remain separately approved operator work, not initialization effects.

1. Confirm the target and identity

Read the root and scoped agent guides. Inspect the actual files listed below, the working tree, and the consumer's Git remote. GitHub copies template files unchanged; the new repository name is only a suggested slug, not approval to rename the project. Missing Git metadata or an unverified repository blocks readiness; report it instead of guessing the target. Preserve unrelated changes.

Read the complete private preparation workbook and resolve the account/operator references from its selected protected profile. Verify identity, permissions, credentials and current operator source/receipt. Missing answers or access produce a private readiness report, not a configuration interview. Prefer scoped authentication so another project's global CLI account stays unchanged.

Validate the written identity answers against these constraints:

InputExampleRule
Project sluginventory-portal3-40 lowercase ASCII letters/digits separated by single hyphens; start with a letter. This satisfies both application names and deployed project paths.
Display nameInventory PortalNonempty human-readable product name. Keep it the same across locales unless localized names are supplied.
Java base packagecom.acme.inventoryExplicit dotted namespace of lowercase ASCII Java identifiers; each segment starts with a letter; exclude Java keywords. This is the application's package, not just its organization prefix.
PWA short nameInventoryUse the display name if it is at most 12 characters; otherwise obtain an approved short name.

Derive these values consistently:

SettingDerivationExample
Frontend package<slug>-frontendinventory-portal-frontend
Gradle root project and Spring application<slug>-backendinventory-portal-backend
Gradle groupJava base packagecom.acme.inventory
Local Compose project<slug>-localinventory-portal-local
Default local database and database userSlug with hyphens replaced by underscoresinventory_portal
Java source directory suffixJava base package with dots replaced by /com/acme/inventory
Java main class<java-base-package>.BackendApplicationcom.acme.inventory.BackendApplication

Escape supplied display names for each destination's JSON, HTML, TypeScript, Groovy, or Markdown syntax rather than interpolating unescaped text.

Done when: the workbook authorizes the validated identity, the live target is this private consumer rather than the canonical template, and current written authority/readiness covers the resolved plan.

2. Establish the data and resume boundary

Check whether the consumer already has an identity recorded in its README or configured in the application. If requested values already match, verify them instead of rewriting. For an incomplete initialization with that same identity, finish only the missing changes. A different existing consumer identity is a later rename: report the boundary and require separately authorized scope. Completed consumers retain their accepted setup; a missing new preparation file does not authorize reinitialization or invalidate existing acceptance.

Check for existing local environment files and Docker resources using names and labels, without printing environment values. Changing the Compose project name changes its generated volume/network names; it does not rename or migrate a database. New database/user settings also do not change an initialized PostgreSQL volume.

For a fresh clone, update the committed environment example before generating local credentials or starting PostgreSQL. If a local database or an existing environment file uses the old identity, report the mismatch and require a written decision before changing identity or starting another database. Preserve existing passwords, volumes, and data. Data migration, volume deletion, and password resets are outside this runbook. Resolve known mismatches during preparation/readiness. A newly discovered mismatch during execution blocks the affected phase until safely reconciled within the approved scope; it is not permission to reset data.

Done when: initialization can proceed without replacing an existing identity or hiding an existing database behind newly generated resource names.

Inspect both repository-derived GHCR package names before authorizing writes. An existing package owned by another repository is a preserve/block boundary, not an implicit takeover. Follow the preparation guide's exact replacement rows, version counts, digest-loss acknowledgement and conditional CLI authorization before any approved deletion. Preserve repositories, credentials and data.

3. Replace application-owned values

The following is the current replacement map. Read each field before editing; if the layout differs, locate its owner and report the difference. Use exact fields and package-prefix changes, not a global replacement of RGO, backend, or vireocode.

Backend and local infrastructure

Paths in this table are relative to the workspace root.

File or surfaceTemplate valueConsumer change
backend/settings.gradlerootProject.name = 'backend'Set <slug>-backend. Keep the physical backend/ folder.
backend/build.gradlegroup = 'com.vireocode'; description VireoCode Web App Starter backendSet group to the approved Java base package and description to <display name> backend. Preserve versions, plugins, and dependencies.
backend/src/main/resources/application.yamlspring.application.name: vireocode-backendSet <slug>-backend. Preserve /api, profiles, datasource placeholders, session/security settings, and Hibernate validation.
backend/compose.yamlname: vireocode-web-app-starter-localSet <slug>-local. Keep the postgres service and postgres-data volume key; Compose scopes their resources by project.
backend/.env.examplePOSTGRES_DB=vireocode; POSTGRES_USER=vireocodeSet both to the underscore-form slug. Keep passwords empty and retain the initial-user defaults unless the user requests different local account details.
backend/src/main/java/ and backend/src/test/java/, each with the template suffix com/vireocode/backend/Package prefix com.vireocode.backendMove all owned Java files into the approved package's directory under each source root; update package declarations, imports, and qualified references. Retain relative auth and user subpackages and the BackendApplication class name.
.vscode/launch.jsonmainClass: com.vireocode.backend.BackendApplicationSet the qualified main class. Omit the optional projectName for this single backend: the IDE import name can differ from Gradle's root name. Preserve both configurations, tasks, working directories and local profile.

Keep the physical frontend/ and backend/ folders, Flyway migration filenames and SQL schema, database table names, and authentication endpoint/DTO contracts unchanged. Delete only empty old Java package directories after all their owned files have moved.

Preserve local ports unless there is a confirmed collision. If a port change is needed, keep its launch/task/proxy and documented references consistent.

Frontend identity
File or surfaceTemplate valueConsumer change
frontend/package.jsonname: rgo-frontend-templateSet <slug>-frontend; retain dependency names and versions.
frontend/package-lock.jsonTop-level name and packages[""].name are rgo-frontend-templateAlign both with the frontend package name. Keep the dependency graph and integrity data unchanged; if using npm to refresh the lockfile, inspect and discard unrelated task-generated churn.
frontend/index.html<title>RGO application</title>Set the display name; retain the app entry point and asset references.
frontend/public/manifest.jsonname: RGO application; short_name: RGOSet the display and approved short names. Preserve id, start_url, scope, and icon entries; naming is not a routing change.
translation.en.ts, translation.hr.ts, development-guide.en.ts, development-guide.hr.tsnavigation.shellTitle contains RGO application or RGO aplikacijaSet the approved display name in all four catalogs. Keep translation keys and localized page labels.
Brand assets

The header's Brand in AppShell.tsx uses alt="RGO" and the bundled RGO symbol assets. The favicon and PWA icons also contain template branding. A new display name alone does not provide new artwork.

If replacement artwork is supplied, update its accessible name, header symbols, favicon, and both installed-app icons together, retaining light/dark readability and valid asset references. If it is not supplied, retain the existing artwork and its accurate alternative text and report branding as deferred. Preserve framework attribution and license notices in either case.

Tests and documentation

Update only identity-dependent expectations in:

  • AppAuthFlow.test.tsx: document-title suffix.
  • application.spec.ts: document-title suffix.
  • documentation.development.spec.ts: English and Croatian document-title suffixes; retain localized page titles.

Search the remaining owned tests for additional identity-dependent expectations. Keep mock identities and demo credentials unchanged: they are authentication fixtures, not project branding.

Update the root README title and introduction for the consumer. Add a compact Project identity section recording the approved slug, display name, Java base package, and PWA short name. Update the frontend README application heading and any consumer-specific build/JAR examples to match the new Gradle artifact name. Keep working setup and verification instructions and retain a link to this runbook. This runbook's template values and example consumer remain reference material; they are not leftovers to replace.

Done when: every mapped surface matches the approved identity or has a specifically reported deferral, and source directories, Java declarations, Gradle identity, launch configuration, and tests agree.

4. Verify the consumer

Use existing tooling and the repository's configured checks. Run commands from the indicated directories; Docker must be available for backend tests.

From backend/:

./gradlew test bootJar

From frontend/:

npm run verify
npm run test:browser -- tests/browser/application.spec.ts --grep 'supports keyboard navigation|offers the account menu' --reporter=list
npm run test:browser:development -- tests/browser/documentation.development.spec.ts --reporter=list

Restore dependencies only when a chosen check reports them missing. Use npm ci for the existing lockfile; keep dependency upgrades outside initialization.

Search tracked/owned application files for the old Java package, package name, Spring/Compose names, and application-title strings. Exclude dependencies, generated build/test output, environment secrets, and Git internals. Classify every residual match: retained runbook examples, framework references, attribution, mock fixtures, or deferred artwork are legitimate. Unexplained application-identity leftovers are incomplete work.

Validate that the Java launch configuration points to the new main class and owned source; keep the frontend launch configuration usable. With VS Code Java tools available, launch through them after project import. If they are unavailable, report the IDE launch check as unverified rather than claiming JSON inspection proves it.

For a fresh local setup, follow the root README's existing credential/database steps. The local credential helper is unrelated to renaming and stays unchanged. Check that the frontend runs in HTTP mode against /api; an existing .env.local may still select mocks. Exercise initial login, refresh, and logout through the real backend, and confirm the visible document/installed-app names. Handle credentials through local files or secret interfaces, not committed documents or the final report. Stop only processes started for verification and retain the local database volume.

Done when: builds/tests pass, the replacement audit has no unexplained leftovers, and local runtime/IDE results are recorded. Missing prerequisites or failed checks are explicit blockers, not successful verification.

5. Configure shared CI access

GitHub's template creation copies repository files, not runner access, variables, secrets, branch protections, or environment settings. Obtain the consumer's exact GitHub owner/repository, approved project slug, and selected shared CI operator. For the organization maintained here, the permanent foundation source belongs to vireocodedev/web-app-starter; experimental repositories are not dependencies.

The detailed install-once and registration procedures live in the shared CI operator guide. Read it before any runner operation. Consumers inherit its source files but register for the existing pool, rather than reinstall it or create an app-specific permanent runner.

Give the operator this nonsecret registration input, substituting the consumer's values:

{
  "slug": "inventory-portal",
  "repository": "your-org/inventory-portal"
}

If the shared host does not yet exist, the operator follows Hetzner provider access to establish a protected project API credential, verified server/image/SSH identity, and exact rebuild scope. This is an install-once bootstrap prerequisite, not a cloud credential requirement for every consumer. Apply those instructions to the selected host; the current template host identifiers in that guide must not be reused blindly.

The operator must verify private repository identity, extend the protected GitHub App installation's selected-repository access, register while the controller is stopped/disabled/idle, and establish a fresh current-boot isolation receipt before an approved activation. The single-repository format is intentional: separate frontend/backend repository fields are not supported. Keep the credential on the controller host, never in the consumer checkout or workflow secrets. Do not request its value in chat. The operator's installed source must already satisfy the reviewed transport, isolation and activation prerequisites. A missing repair or privileged-source upgrade blocks consumer readiness and belongs to a separately approved operator change. Preserve certificate verification, memory limits, isolated Python imports and the worker trust boundary. Historical template receipts do not establish current source/configuration/boot-bound consumer readiness. Follow GitHub CI App setup for the organization-owned App, minimal permissions, protected PEM/metadata, automatic token renewal, and guarded credential-free adapter preparation. Do not substitute a personal token into the permanent controller interface. If credential rotation removes repository access, preserve any registration/job recovery evidence; an authorization-related 404 does not prove a runner was removed. Follow the operator guide's interrupted-job recovery procedure.

Workflows route to [self-hosted, Linux, X64, web-app-ci], with read-only PR token permissions and no production/registry-write credentials. Labels select jobs; the protected allowlist and repository-scoped JIT runners authorize repository access. An empty GitHub runner inventory while idle is expected for this disposable pool; verify a genuine job instead of installing a permanent runner just to make that page nonempty.

Keep this app's Java 21 toolchain. The immutable worker baseline also contains Node/npm and a validation JDK; select Java 21 inside the backend job using the job-local tool cache described in the operator guide. Backend commands must run from backend/, frontend commands from frontend/. Only root .github/workflows/ files execute in this monorepo; nested frontend workflow examples do not establish active CI.

Verify the operator's current boot/source/configuration receipt, register this consumer and repeat required validation. Record actual consumer workflow/check names, run URLs and GitHub settings in its setup documentation rather than treating configured labels or historical template acceptance as working CI.

Done when: the consumer's runner access is registered and current host acceptance plus genuine repository CI are verified, or the precise pending operator/workflow prerequisites are reported. Do not rebuild a host, enable services, publish, or deploy as a side effect of identity personalization. Full-mode registration/activation and deployments follow their explicit approved contract and operator gates instead.

6. Configure GitHub CI and main protection

Follow Monorepo CI and main protection for root workflow paths, change-selection rules, exact required-check naming, and the settings that GitHub does not copy from a template. Keep the shared Hetzner runner selection; changing a custom label also requires its operator registration and the actionlint label configuration.

Verify actual consumer backend-only, frontend-only, both-owner, and unrelated PR results before claiming CI is working. Protect the selected integration branch after the real CI gate check succeeds: require PRs with zero approving reviews, bind the required check to GitHub Actions, require up-to-date branches, enforce for administrators, and block force pushes/deletion. Record observed run URLs, runner identity, effective policy, and a blocked/green mergeability test. Keep publication/deployment credentials separate from PR jobs. Omit unused reviewer and wait-timer fields when creating the default GitHub environments; an explicit empty reviewer list can request unsupported private-plan protection. Verify the resulting empty rules without an implicit paid upgrade.

Done when: the correct checks run on the consumer's authorized Hetzner pool and the effective main policy is verified, or a concrete access/plan/run blocker is reported. Copied workflow files alone are not activation evidence.

7. Establish environment DNS access

Obtain the consumer's exact production and staging hostnames and inspect their authoritative nameservers and existing A/AAAA/CNAME records. Keep one HTTPS origin per environment and the backend at /api. Consumers supply their own names and selected host addresses; template hostnames are not defaults.

Follow DNS project access for the exact existing zone, provider credential boundary, guarded record writes, and authoritative/recursive checks. A Cloud server token is not automatically authorized for a zone in another project. Obtain the correct protected credential rather than creating a duplicate zone or changing delegation.

Current gate: both template A records were created and verified against all authoritative nameservers and two public recursive resolvers using the correct DNS-project credential. DNS acceptance records the exact changes. Local recursive NXDOMAIN was still observed at inspection time; resolver/cache readiness is separate from successful authoritative writes. The template's later container, routing, public TLS and backup activation is recorded separately in release acceptance; DNS alone did not certify those outcomes.

Done when: the intended records are verified at the selected existing authoritative zone, with conflicts resolved and access/negative-cache blockers reported. DNS success alone does not certify HTTPS or a deployed application.

8. Prepare whole-app release images

Follow paired release setup. Keep separate frontend/backend image boundaries but one matched release from the selected tested commit. Supply the actual repository URL/source SHA, build both pinned Dockerfiles, and run the restricted image smoke tests before publication. Preserve the frontend's same-origin /api build configuration so staging and production can use the same immutable image pair. Environment hostnames, DB credentials, and production users belong in protected deployment provisioning, not Docker contexts/images.

The current CI builds/smoke-tests each selected owner image independently. The two manual entrypoints are Deploy staging and Deploy production, without a component dropdown. Staging verifies/builds/publishes the pair; production promotes the exact successful staging pair without rebuilding and requires the same selected source SHA. Follow operator installation and activation for all affected host files, workflow IDs, maintainer allowlist, public DEPLOY_CONTROLLER_CERT variable, protected App/DB/account credentials, port allocation, Caddy, backup schedule, source pins and recovery safeguards. Do not place server credentials in PR CI or widen its host/private-network access. Root execution validates actual manual run identity, not runner labels.

For initial deployed accounts, follow one-time operator provisioning. Use the workbook's deliberate consumer account decision and separately generated protected credentials rather than automatically seeding deployed users. Use the current backend digest, existing DB network, separate PROVISION_USER_* settings and explicit --provision-user command under the environment lock; verify termination, repeat safety and real HTTPS login. Keep provisioning credentials out of normal app containers and preserve conflicts rather than resetting users.

Use the consumer's explicit backup destination/risk decision and daily time/timezone rather than inheriting a template exception or schedule. Retention stays 30 days and staging remains unscheduled. Deployment, public TLS, account installation, and initialized backup restoration require the linked operator steps and actual acceptance; source implementation is not proof that the corresponding host/remote settings exist.

Done when: the exact committed image pair passes real restricted runtime checks and its immutable provenance is known, or the precise build/platform blocker is reported. Working containers alone are not GHCR/deployment evidence.

Follow deployment operation and recovery rehearsal for ongoing actions. Accounts, protected secret files, public certificate variables, remote settings, host registration and backup evidence are specific to each consumer, not inherited from historical template receipts.

9. Report the result

Return the approved identity, changed surfaces, commands and outcomes, and any blocked checks or deferred artwork. Point to local setup instructions without revealing credentials. For personalization-only scope, leave changes uncommitted unless a commit is requested; publication/deployment need separate approval. For full /initialize-project scope, perform the approved commits/PRs and remote actions, and require every acceptance phase in the contract before reporting ready. Record consumer-specific evidence, not copied template receipts. Include the shared CI registration/verification state without treating a template copy as inherited GitHub access.

Done when: the consumer can distinguish completed personalization, verified full initialization, and blocked/remaining work without relying on a generic "setup complete" claim. Unverified required checks cannot be waived by reporting.

Project documentation dashboard

The skill owns the generic preparation, contract, runbook and rehearsal lessons. Keep consumer identity, operating instructions and sanitized acceptance under docs/; keep private inputs and readiness reports under ignored .template-initialization/. The short docs/template-initialization.md entry point links here instead of duplicating the generic procedure. Add consumer-specific setup decisions there when needed.

Documentation generation has its own dependency graph and lockfile:

npm --prefix .github/skills/initialize-project ci
npm --prefix .github/skills/initialize-project run browser:install
npm --prefix .github/skills/initialize-project run docs:build
npm --prefix .github/skills/initialize-project run verify
npm --prefix .github/skills/initialize-project run test:portable-install

Browser tests use the skill's pinned Playwright and Chromium, with isolated temporary consumer worktrees and synthetic answers. Browser installation is a test prerequisite only; the wizard itself needs neither Playwright nor npm. CI installs the browser under its disposable runner temporary directory. The portable-install check copies only the skill into a temporary Git worktree, installs its own lockfile and verifies generated docs and browser flows. Template-only application/CI/receipt/pointer tests are explicitly inapplicable there; the full template verification still requires them.

After editing any bundled reference, top-level docs/*.md or docs/acceptance/*-acceptance.json, regenerate and commit both derived pages: docs/project.html combines public consumer sources and skill references; web/reference.html in the skill includes only bundled references. Neither loads private state or remote assets. The reference page remains unrecorded/not ready, even when a consumer's dashboard reports completion.

The wizard needs no npm dependencies. A portable installation copies only this skill directory (excluding node_modules) into .github/skills/ of a consumer, adds /.template-initialization/ to its Git ignore rules and runs the Node entry point. Full initialization still requires the template's application, infrastructure guides and operator prerequisites; portability of the human input tool does not make unrelated applications supported consumers.

Done when: isolated skill tests and documentation freshness checks pass; private inputs are excluded, reference links work, and consumer status comes only from that consumer's acceptance evidence.

.github/skills/initialize-project/references/preparation.md

Prepare a consumer before initialization

Procedure

Prepare a consumer before initialization

Prepare before invoking /initialize-project, preferably through the guided local web app below. It replaces the configuration interview with short browser steps and a private Markdown workbook saved for the skill. The contract owns verification and authority; the runbook owns application edits and operator procedures. This document owns the human preparation steps and answers.

This is a blank, reusable template, not evidence that any consumer is prepared. An already completed consumer does not need to be initialized again.

0. Use the guided local web app

From the consumer Git worktree root, with Node 24 and Git available on Linux:

node .github/skills/initialize-project/scripts/prepare.mjs

No frontend, dependency installation or application server is needed. The installed skill locates its own assets/references and defaults to that consumer root, independently of the terminal directory. To select another Git worktree, pass --root /absolute/path/to/consumer; --no-open leaves browser opening to you. The private directory must be ignored by Git before startup.

Keep that terminal running. The local-only server opens a protected browser launcher, then walks through small steps: identity, operator references, GitHub/App consent, package ownership, DNS, account, backups, bounds and authorization. Each step explains what to do and links to the relevant service. Use Back, the step list, or Do this later to work in your own order. Incomplete items remain visible at final review.

Drafts automatically save to ignored .template-initialization/preparation-draft.json, mode 0600 under a user-owned 0700 directory. Restarting the command restores the draft/step. An existing valid Markdown workbook can be imported; it is not overwritten without your explicit replacement confirmation and a matching file revision. Changing answers clears the final review confirmation. Signing timestamps are set only by your input or an explicit time-button click, never auto-approved.

At final review, Save private workbook writes .template-initialization/preparation.md atomically. That is the same input consumed by /initialize-project; you do not need to edit Markdown. A planning request may retain unresolved inputs; execution requires the complete scope, attestations, valid values and a current explicit signature.

The browser app binds only to 127.0.0.1, uses an unguessable per-run access path and rejects cross-origin writes. Open the private .template-initialization/preparation-launch.html if automatic browser opening is unavailable. The launcher/session file contains a temporary local access link: do not share it, commit it or place it in chat. Answers are not stored in browser local storage or sent to providers. The server does not read arbitrary referenced files, execute the displayed commands, log into services, deploy, or alter existing initialization state. External service links open only when you choose them.

Stop the server with Ctrl+C. Drafts and saved workbooks remain private; only that server's owned launcher/session/lock files are removed. An unexpected stale lock is reported rather than deleted blindly: verify the recorded PID in .template-initialization/preparation-server.lock before removing only a stale lock. Already initialized checkouts show a warning and retain their accepted setup; use a different consumer checkout for another project.

The remaining sections are the detailed reference and manual fallback.

1. Make your private working copy

From the new consumer's workspace root on the supported Linux setup:

umask 077
mkdir -p .template-initialization
chmod 700 .template-initialization
set -C
node .github/skills/initialize-project/scripts/prepare.mjs --template > .template-initialization/preparation.md
chmod 600 .template-initialization/preparation.md

This copying step is unnecessary when using the web app. If a manual copy already exists, keep its answers and update it instead of replacing it. Fill that ignored copy, not this tracked template. Both locations have working links to the shipped guides. The template-export command relocates links for the private destination and supplies blank fields only; it does not sign or authorize anything. Shell no-clobber mode (set -C) preserves an existing workbook.

Never put passwords, tokens, PEM contents, recovery codes, database dumps or secret environment values in either Markdown file. Enter service credentials through the service's own login or a hidden terminal/secret-store mechanism. Record protected file/tool references only. The private workbook and the agent's .template-initialization/readiness.md report are excluded from the public documentation dashboard and from Git. CI lints the tracked template's unfilled answers/approvals even on documentation-only changes. Keep your filled copy private; do not turn the shared template into a saved execution approval.

Replace every REQUIRED answer below. Keep use-profile only where explicitly offered: it means resolve and verify that field from the selected protected operator profile, not guess a template value. Check applicable preparation items only after completing them. An unchecked conditional item must have its documented not-required answer, not an unexplained blank. For plan-only, unknown answers and unsigned approval fields may remain unfilled: they are reported as unresolved, never treated as execution authority. Use table escaping for a literal | in a value; formatting escapes are not part of the product name or other destination value.

2. Prepare GitHub access and App consent

  1. At https://github.com/vireocodedev/web-app-starter, choose Use this template, select the intended owner and create a private consumer repository. Clone it; keep the monorepo and template stack.
  2. In your own terminal, run gh auth status. Log in through gh auth login --hostname github.com --web if necessary. With multiple existing logins, select the intended account yourself using gh auth switch --hostname github.com --user YOUR_ACCOUNT. The agent will verify identity and access, preferably without changing the global account. A signed-in browser and CLI are separate sessions.
  3. Open https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY/settings/actions. Under Actions -> General, ensure the repository can run the template's pinned Actions. Confirm you can administer this private repository and its main policy. Required checks/PRs with zero approving reviews need plan support; making the repository public is not a workaround.
  4. Ask the existing operator for its protected profile and the exact shared App installation. Open https://github.com/organizations/OWNER/settings/installations, choose that existing App's Configure, select Only select repositories, add this consumer and Save, preserving all prior selections.
  5. If your organization restricts that action, have its authorized owner finish it now. Repository-admin CLI access alone did not establish this permission in the rehearsal. Keep the reviewed permissions: Actions: read, Administration: write, and Metadata: read. Do not choose all repositories, expand permissions or create another App for this consumer.

The agent still proves actual selected-repository App authentication and registration permissions. A checked box or a CLI repository read is not proof. It will configure main protection after observing the genuine CI gate, not require you to invent a check before the first CI run. It also creates default staging/production GitHub environments without unnecessary paid reviewer/wait-timer features.

See CI App access and main protection.

3. Resolve existing package names before authorizing changes

The package names derive from the repository, not the application slug: ghcr.io/owner/repository-frontend and -backend.

  1. Open https://github.com/orgs/OWNER/packages and inspect both derived names. You can read exact IDs, owners and version counts without exposing tokens:

    gh api orgs/OWNER/packages/container/REPOSITORY-frontend
gh api orgs/OWNER/packages/container/REPOSITORY-backend

  2. If absent, select require-absent below. If already owned by this same consumer during a resume, select same-repository-resume and preserve them.

  3. For another repository's packages, stop and choose a different consumer repository name, reconcile ownership separately, or explicitly list the exact replacement scope below. An old application/database is not permission to take over its packages. The normal default preserves and blocks.

  4. Only if you approve listed deletion, authorize the active CLI account through GitHub's own browser flow:

    gh auth refresh --hostname github.com --scopes delete:packages

    Do not send the token to the agent or place it in the workbook. This scope is unnecessary for a fresh namespace. The agent rechecks package IDs, repository ownership, privacy, version counts and authority before deleting.

Deleting old versions makes their image digests unavailable to other deployments. Repository deletion, database deletion and password resets are never implied. No deletion is performed merely because this guide is opened.

4. Prepare the existing operator and DNS access

Obtain an existing protected operator profile from the authorized operator. Reuse verified credential references instead of setting up the host again. The profile contract defines its fields, ownership and 0600/private-directory requirements.

The operator must already have a reviewed shared pool, a source/config/boot-bound validation receipt, strictly verified SSH access, an approved deployment host, DNS access to the correct zone/project, and a supported backup destination. Interactive SSH recovery, unknown host keys, an unsupported backup transport or an unreviewed host repair must be resolved by the operator before invocation. This workbook does not authorize a host rebuild, pool install or privileged upgrade.

For Hetzner DNS:

  1. Open https://console.hetzner.com/ and select the existing project that owns the DNS zone, then its DNS zone/records page. A server-project token is not automatically authorized for a zone in a different project.
  2. Confirm ownership/delegation of the zone and choose two distinct hostnames. Inspect A, AAAA and CNAME records and wildcard effects. Preserve matching records. Resolve conflicting ownership with the operator rather than create another zone, change delegation or overwrite unrelated records.
  3. For user-prepared, create only the two intended records pointing at the operator-approved host and let DNS propagate. For agent-create-missing, leave creation to the agent under the exact written scope below; your manual prerequisite is usable authority/credential references, not doing its work.
  4. If a suitable credential does not exist, the zone owner uses that project's Security -> API tokens to create the necessary scoped credential and stores it through protected input. Supply only its profile/file reference. Reuse a suitable existing credential; do not replace the server credential.

The provider handoff contains operator details. Its template host/zone IDs and hostnames are historical examples, not values to copy. The agent verifies provider identity, all authoritative/recursive answers, record conflicts and current capacity. You do not have to create DB volumes, install controllers, publish certificates or run deployments manually.

5. Prepare the local workspace, not an old-identity database

Install the README prerequisites: JDK 21, Node 24/npm 12, Docker/Compose and the recommended Java/Gradle debugger extensions. Open the consumer as a trusted VS Code workspace, complete any extension consent and allow the Gradle import to finish.

Do not generate old-template credentials, start its database or mark the future personalized application as tested. Identity edits must precede fresh credentials/data creation. The agent preserves existing files/volumes and checks port ownership before allocating any approved free port.

Actual IDE acceptance happens after personalization. Before bulk work the agent must identify a usable unattended tool path for both saved configurations, including the frontend's node-terminal launch. Merely seeing Java tools is insufficient. If that path is unavailable, it reports a preparation blocker; it does not promise a no-follow-up run or silently substitute a shell-only test. Unexpected runtime failures still block their gate and are diagnosed within scope; paperwork cannot pre-verify a program that has not been personalized.

6. Fill the answers

The field IDs are stable input labels. Enter literal values or the choices shown, never shell commands. Read the identity constraints before selecting names.

FieldYour answerMeaning
form_version1Workbook format, not permission.
repositoryREQUIREDExact private owner/repository; the agent discovers/verifies numeric ID.
github_accountuse-profileExisting protected CLI login, or exact account.
operator_profileREQUIREDProtected external JSON path/reference; no secret values.
reuse_existing_operatorREQUIREDyes; another foundation/bootstrap is separate work.
allow_global_cli_switchnoPrefer scoped authentication; change only if explicitly yes.

pwa_short_nameREQUIREDAt most 12 characters.

staging_hostnameREQUIREDDifferent owned staging FQDN.
dns_modeREQUIREDuser-prepared or agent-create-missing; conflicts always preserve and block.

Passwords are intentionally absent from the form. The agent generates distinct local/staging/production credentials into protected files after identity personalization, and provisions deployed users explicitly. Choose an authorization window covering the intended bounded run; expiry is not renewed automatically. If it expires, preserve completed work and renew the declaration before further mutations.

Exact optional registry replacement

Leave this table with no data rows unless registry_policy is replace-listed-only. In that case add each authorized package, numeric ID, current owner repository and complete version count. Unknown/new versions or changed ownership block deletion and require a written scope update.

Exact package nameNumeric package IDCurrent owner/repositoryAll versions to delete

Even when replacement is approved, preserve old GitHub repositories, every database/volume, all other packages and every unrelated workload.

7. Mark human prerequisites actually completed

  • Private consumer created/cloned; exact repository and fresh/resume boundary entered.
  • Intended GitHub account is authenticated in the protected CLI store.
  • Repository administration, private Actions and required-check plan support confirmed.
  • Existing shared App has this selected repository; owner/browser consent saved.
  • Existing protected operator profile is available; host trust/source/receipt and capacity are the operator's responsibility.
  • Correct DNS zone/project authority is available; names/conflicts and chosen record-creation mode resolved.
  • Package names inspected; no conflict, same-consumer resume, or exact replacement rows and digest-loss acknowledgement recorded.
  • Conditional delete:packages authorization completed, or registry_delete_auth is not-required because no deletion is requested.
  • Local tools, Docker and trusted VS Code/Java import/extension consent prepared.
  • Identity, artwork, account, backup destination/risk/schedule and allocation bounds answered.

These are human attestations for preflight, not substitutes for the agent's authenticated checks or post-personalization/runtime/restore evidence.

8. Authorize the bounded execution in writing

For plan-only, the agent performs read-only discovery and writes a readiness report; it does not execute the actions below.

For execute-listed-scope, check every action you actually authorize. A missing required action blocks full initialization rather than creating a partial success. Fill signer/timestamps above yourself. By invoking /initialize-project after completing this workbook, you make the current request to execute only the listed scope if live preflight matches it:

  • Personalize this consumer's approved identity/assets and generate protected distinct credentials.
  • Build/test, launch the real native/IDE/browser flows and allocate only approved unused local ports.
  • Register this exact repository through the existing reviewed operator at an idle maintenance point; validate before reactivation and preserve existing registrations.
  • Create scoped consumer commits/branches/PRs/pushes and configure main with the genuine CI gate, strict PRs, zero approving reviews and administrator enforcement.
  • Use only the declared DNS names, existing host/namespace and permitted free ports; preserve matching records and block conflicts.
  • Prepare isolated consumer databases/volumes/networks/controller/TLS and publish only the public controller certificate variable.
  • Run real Deploy staging and promote its exact successful immutable pair with Deploy production at the same selected source.
  • Explicitly provision the approved users, verify both real HTTPS/browser flows, retrieve and isolated-restore an initialized production dump, then enable only the approved production schedule.
  • Remove only exact task-owned scratch containers/temporary transfer or credential files; retain protected backups and all unrelated resources.
  • If and only if exact replacement rows are present and approved above, replace only those packages/versions; otherwise no old image/package deletion.

The final replacement checkbox is conditional: leave it unchecked when there are no replacement rows and the deletion fields are not-required. That is not a missing mandatory approval and grants no deletion authority.

Fixed exclusions: no upstream publication, new paid host, resize/rebuild, shared privileged-source upgrade, repository deletion, database replacement, password reset or live-database restore. A workbook cannot override these workflow boundaries or mandatory tool/provider approvals.

The profile, checked boxes and old state are not standing permission. The current user invocation, complete signed/unexpired workbook, matching verified consumer and resolved in-scope plan must agree. The agent records the workbook SHA-256 and approval provenance before mutations and never fills your approval fields for you.

9. Invoke once prepared

Open a fresh agent chat in this trusted consumer workspace and invoke:

/initialize-project

The skill reads .template-initialization/preparation.md, discovers/verifies facts, and writes a nonsecret .template-initialization/readiness.md containing the resolved plan, checks, missing fields and exact blockers. Within your written bounds it proceeds without a chat questionnaire or another routine configuration/approval round.

If missing/expired/conflicting input, access or tool capability blocks the gate, read that report, complete the named manual steps, amend/re-sign the private workbook and invoke again. The agent does not edit your answers, claim checkboxes as proof, reset data, or bypass provider prompts. A new scope, cost or destructive decision needs written authorization before affected work. Stable-mode reusable-learning proposals likewise require explicit written proposal IDs; none leaves those edits unapproved while otherwise authorized operations may continue.

No filled copy is required merely to explain/maintain this skill or to verify an already completed consumer without mutations. Existing accepted completion evidence is preserved; adopting this workbook does not rerun completed setup.

Sources: GitHub App installation/access and GitHub CLI scope refresh.

Rehearsal lessons

Procedure

Rehearsal lessons

These are generic prevention rules from an earlier consumer rehearsal, not acceptance evidence for this template or another consumer. A clean fresh-consumer run is still required to prove the complete no-follow-up initialization experience.

Observed bottleneckRequired prevention
CLI identity differed from the repository ownerSelect the protected account/profile before invocation; verify access and prefer scoped authentication.
Existing application/database identity was ambiguousRecord fresh versus same-identity resume and preserve existing resources.
Identity, artwork, accounts and backup risk needed human decisionsCollect explicit workbook answers before bulk changes.
Operator/profile discovery happened lateArrange the existing operator reference and verify current source, trust, receipt and capacity upfront.
Selected-repository App access needed owner browser consentComplete the existing App's saved repository selection beforehand; repository administration alone is not proof.
Old image namespaces belonged to different repositoriesInspect package ownership, preserve by default and require exact deletion rows, version counts and digest-loss consent.
Approved package deletion lacked CLI scopeComplete GitHub's conditional native authorization before invocation.
Port defaults collided with another applicationVerify ownership and allocate only approved unused ports; update all dependent surfaces.
IDE import name differed from Gradle identityOmit the optional single-backend projectName; verify the actual saved launch after personalization.
Generic Java launch did not prove saved IDE launchesVerify an unattended tool path for both configurations during readiness, then test real launches.
Empty reviewer settings invoked unavailable private-plan featuresOmit unused protection fields and verify actual readback; do not upgrade plans implicitly.
A Python isolation flag hid an installed CLI's sibling modulesUse the operator-documented interpreter/entrypoint; verify --help and real backup behavior.
A transient container startup failed CIKeep the failing required check; diagnose/retry within scope without weakening isolation.

Human login/2FA, App consent, credential entry, identity/risk choices and written authority remain human tasks. The wizard collects preparation; only live verification can establish runtime, CI, deployment and initialized recovery acceptance. Unexpected post-intake assistance is a preparation defect to record, not a reason to claim a no-follow-up success.
